Lesson No. 235: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 1 to 23
Verses 1 to 5

Ha. Mim. After these letters, it is stated that this Book is from Allah, the Mighty and the Wise, and that the source and origin of this Book is the Being of Allah. Another indication in this is that this miraculous Book has been composed from these very letters, as is our view regarding the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters at the beginning of certain surahs), and that it is a challenge to them that you cannot compose such a Book from these letters. Therefore, Ha. Mim. is an evidence for the sending down of the Book, that it is from Allah, and that Allah is possessed of overwhelming power and no one can contend with Him, and He is Wise, who created this entire universe with wisdom, and all affairs are decided by the command of that Being. This is a comment that is suitable to the atmosphere of the surah, in which various kinds of souls and their mentalities are shown.

Before presenting the position of the people regarding this Book, they are directed to those signs and proofs which lie scattered throughout this universe. These signs and proofs were sufficient for these people to believe, and if they had turned their hearts towards them, their hearts would have opened, and their awareness of the great Allah who revealed this Book, who is the great Creator of this universe, would have been heightened.

Verily, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers (45:3). "Indeed, in the heavens and the earth there are countless signs for those who believe." And the signs that are in the heavens and the earth are not confined to any one thing, nor to any one state. Whatever thing of this universe a person sees and studies, the heart bears witness that this very aspect is a miracle, as if to say, "Wherever you go, it is here." The question is not where the sign is; the question is, which thing is not a sign?

Look at these heavens and the great celestial bodies swimming within them, then at their vast and wide expanses; they are spread out like particles and mustard seeds, in comparison with that space, and that frightfully vast and wide space. And they are extremely beautiful.

Then look at how continuous the revolution of these bodies is in their respective orbits. With extremely beautiful harmony, a person wishes to keep on looking and is never satisfied with observing them. Some revolutions are completed in millions of years, and there is not a difference of even one second.

And this earth, which a person considers very vast and wide, is an extremely small particle in comparison with those great stars (only Jupiter is a thousand times bigger than it). Then this particle, that is the earth, is floating within this vast space of the universe. If it were not for the power of Allah, who has held it and confined it in its orbit, it would lose its way in this boundless space; but it is the perfection of Allah's power that not even a particle of this universe can get lost here.

Then the provisions that Allah has placed on this earth, owing to its particular position and system, and due to which life has become possible upon it, every aspect of that is a sign. Every element of this provision, with its own properties, has been gathered here with great precision, in great abundance and harmony. If the property or nature of any one element were to change even slightly, the entire system of life would be disrupted or would be completely destroyed. In short, every living thing on this earth is a separate sign. Every single part and every single organ of each thing is a separate sign. In this matter, large objects and particles of dust alike are signs. Take a small leaf from a great tree, or take a small plant from the vast expanses of this universe, and examine it: in its form and its design, it is a sign, both in its color and in its smallness; a sign for its purposes and a sign in its body. Take even a single hair of a human being or an animal; this too is a sign; its composition and its color are signs. Every feather of every bird is a sign; its material composition, its purposes, and its harmony. If a person looks at this earth and heaven with the eye of insight, he will see a throng of divine signs, and he will declare that all these signs are beyond his thought and vision.

But for whom are these signs? The verses themselves make it clear: for whom are these signs a veil, and who can perceive them? Surely (there are signs) for a people who have certainty (45:4), "for those who have certainty." It is the believer who sees by the light of his Lord.

Thus, it is faith alone that is the power which opens the doors of hearts. Then a person hears the call; some light can enter the hearts and illuminate them; some fresh breezes can scatter freshness over the world of the heart. And it is through faith alone that a person can see the signs scattered everywhere in this universe. It is faith that grants the hearts such refreshing delight, and creates in them tenderness and sensitivity, as a result of which these hearts receive the indications that are coming from every direction in this universe, which show that these indications are from the hand of power, and that whatever the hand of power creates contains these indications within it. Every thing created by Allah is a miracle, and creation cannot even imitate it. Now, bringing a person back from the long and far-off valleys of this universe, he is brought to his own self, which is closest to him. And there is a call to reflect on the animals that are near to human beings!

And in your own creation... and in the animals which Allah has spread throughout the earth, there are great signs for a people who have certainty (45:4), "And in your own creation and in the living creatures which He has scattered through the earth are signs for people who have certainty." To grant a person this wondrous structure, then to grant him such wondrous qualities, and to entrust to him extremely deep, subtle and complex functions, each of which is miraculous. There are such inner miracles of the human body that, having seen them day and night, they have not ceased to be wonders for us, because they are within us and near us. But if even a single organ were to be examined, a person's head would spin, and he would remain stunned by the horrors of that intricate composition.

Life, even in its simplest form, is itself a miracle. The amoeba, which has only one cell, and life even smaller than the amoeba, is also a miracle. As for man, his life is very intricate, harsh and wondrous. Psychologically too, he is extremely complex and miraculous. His psychology is more complex than his physical composition.

And the creatures that crawl all over this earth, which are of countless kinds and types, with innumerable bodies and forms, the number of which is known only to Allah. Among this life, the smallest thing and the largest thing, all are miraculous in their own place; they possess a miraculous character both in their life-span and in their species. They naturally protect their species, and no species is capable of destroying other species. And the hand of power has kept the count of these kinds and types in its own hand: it decreases some and increases others. And it gives each one its characteristics and its capacity and ability. In this way, a balance is maintained within the population of all kinds and types of animals.

Vultures and hawks are aggressive and harmful birds, and their lifespan is also long, but their population is very small and they lay very few eggs. If vultures and hawks were like sparrows, just consider that perhaps no species of bird, big or small, would survive in this world.

Among animals, lions are predatory beasts. If their progeny were as numerous as deer, sheep and goats, they would leave no animal matter in the forests. But it is the power of nature that has kept their progeny limited, and they exist only in the required number, whereas deer, sheep and goats are numerous, because nature knows that there is greater need for them.

A single housefly lays millions of eggs in one lifetime, but its life is at most two weeks. If the natural lifespan of a housefly were several months or years, they would cover all human bodies and devour the eyes; but the hand of power has also placed a natural restraint upon them and limited their lifespan.

Similarly, this is the condition of every thing and every species. The planning and decree of Allah works among humans and animals, and within everything there is a kind of sign. And this sign cries out, saying that you should reflect and ponder upon the signs of Allah, and these signs are for a people who have certainty (45:4).

Certainty is a state which makes hearts ready, inclined and affected, so that they may perceive, be affected and incline towards Allah. Faith and certainty make hearts steadfast, firm and content. Such hearts reflect upon this universe with great tranquility and derive truths from it. Restlessness, anxiety and instability disappear from them. Even if such hearts obtain little in this world, they derive from it greater results and effects.

After this, from their own selves and the animals around them, they are led to the manifestations of this whole universe. Reflect upon the means of life that are created and provided from this universe for them and for other living beings.

And in the alternation of night and day, and in the provision which Allah sends down from the sky, and by which He revives the dead earth... and in the changing of the winds there are signs for a people who use reason (45:5), "And in the alternation of night and day, and in the provision which Allah sends down from the heaven, and with it gives life to the earth after its death, and in the variation of the winds are signs for a people who understand." The revolution of night and day is a scene whose novelty is erased from human minds because of its repeated recurrence. If someone sees it for the first time, or sees the night for the first time, it is a wondrous sight; those whose hearts possess a poetic sensibility perceive this novelty and regard the revolution of night and day as a bewildering system of this universe.

Human knowledge keeps increasing, and humans have now gained extensive information about some of the phenomena of this universe. Now people know that the revolution of night and day actually arises from the axial rotation of the earth, which it performs facing the sun, and this rotation is completed in twenty-four hours. But even according to this knowledge, this wondrous scene and marvel has not ended, because this earth is suspended in the air and is moving at a certain speed, and it does not rest on anything. Allah has held it, and it does not reduce its speed even for a second. And this speed is such that all living creatures live very comfortably upon it, and this creation rests upon a globe suspended in space that is in motion in the atmosphere.

Now human knowledge expands somewhat further, to discover the effects of this axial rotation upon this earth and upon all living creatures. Humans have discovered that it is only by dividing time into night and day in this manner that life has been made possible on this planet. If there were no alternation of night and day, or if they were not in this measure, system and speed, everything on the surface of this earth would change, and especially human life would come to an end. Thus, after this knowledge, it became clear that the alternation of night and day is among the important signs of Allah.

And in the provision which Allah sends down from the heaven, and with it gives life to the dead earth (45:5), "And in the provision which Allah sends down from the heaven, and with it revives the dead lands." Provision here is generally understood by classical exegetes to mean water which descends from the sky. But that which descends from the heavens is far broader than water alone. The rays which emanate from the heavens are no less effective than water in giving life to the earth; indeed, it is through the effect of these rays, by the command of Allah, that water comes into being. It is the heat of the sun which turns water into vapour. These vapours condense and take the form of rain, and rivers and springs flow. And thereby the earth, after being dead, becomes alive, both by water and by heat.

And in the variation of the winds (45:5), "and in the changing of the winds." These winds blow north and south, blow east and west, blow straight and crooked, blow hot and cold. In accordance with this extremely intricate system which the hand of power has placed within the creation of this universe, and every thing of which it has arranged by measure and reckoning, and in which it has left nothing to chance or to neglect, the blowing of the winds is closely linked to the axial rotation of the earth. And they are linked also to the alternation of night and day, and to that provision which descends from the heavens. In short, the system of heat, wind, and night and day all work together here, and in them are signs and proofs. For a people who understand (45:5), "for a people who use reason," because in this field only reason can operate.

These, then, are some of the signs of this universe to which attention has been drawn, for those who believe; then for those who have certainty; and then for those who use reason. These verses point to them. These indications touch hearts, awaken them, and these divine verses address human nature directly, because between human nature and this universe there is a direct natural connection. And it is only the Qur'anic style of reasoning that can revive and refresh this connection. Those who do not acknowledge these signs of nature cannot be expected to acknowledge anything else. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 45, verses 7–10:

Verses 7 to 10

As we explained in the introduction to this surah, the verses depict how the polytheists of Makkah received the Islamic call. They insisted upon their false position. They refused to listen to even a single word of a true call that was based upon the truth and that was clear in its own nature. The arrival of the call was itself the proof, like the sun is its own proof. They were so stubborn in refusing to accept this truth that it appeared as though the call had never reached their minds. Rather, they became insolent toward Allah, and they began to turn away from the verses of the Qur'an that reached them. The Qur'an severely condemned this attitude of theirs and gave them a stern warning: woe to them, and they shall suffer a humiliating and painful punishment.

﴿Woe to every lying, sinful wrongdoer﴾ (45:7). Woe (wayl) means destruction. Affak means one who is a great liar, skilled in fabricating falsehood, and one who gathers a great deal of sin and immorality. This warning applies to every person who possesses these qualities. It is the warning of Allah, the Subduer, the Compeller, who has power to destroy and ruin, and whose warnings, threats and admonitions are entirely true. Therefore, the threat given in this phrase is extremely frightening.

What is the characteristic and sign of such a liar, a sinner and an evildoer? It is that he insists upon falsehood, instead of bowing before the truth he is arrogant; instead of acknowledging the signs of Allah he turns away from them, and he does not adopt a respectful attitude but rather behaves with insolence.

﴿He hears the verses of Allah being recited to him, then persists in his disbelief with full arrogance, as though he had not heard them﴾ (45:8). This is a most detestable picture. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 45, verses 12–13:

Verses 12 to 13

This small creature, man, is the recipient of Allah's great favour, for He has subjected to him the great creations of this universe. Man benefits from these creations in various ways, and Allah has taught him the law of nature governing this universe, according to which it runs and from which it cannot deviate. Had Allah not given man such capacity for knowledge, it would not have been possible for him to subdue these cosmic forces and benefit from them in this way. Rather, it would have become difficult for him even to live amid those forces, because man is a tiny insect, while the forces of nature are extremely powerful, enormously massive, and vast celestial bodies.

The sea is one of those great forces that man has subdued. Allah gave man knowledge of its nature and properties, and man discovered that a ship can move over this vast and wild sea, can clash with its raging, tyrannical waves, and can suffer no harm from them.

﴿That the ships may sail therein by His command﴾ (45:12). It is Allah who gave the sea these properties and gave the material of the ship the property of floating. He created the properties of air pressure, the force of winds, and the attraction of the earth, and placed in them other properties by which sea travel became easy, and He gave man the knowledge to derive benefit from the sea's creatures and to obtain its other benefits.

﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (45:12). For example, hunting in the sea, materials of adornment, trade, journeys of knowledge, experiments, exercise, recreation, and so on. In short, all the benefits that this small human being obtains from the seas.

In short, Allah subjected the ship and the sea to man so that he might seek Allah's bounty. Then he should thank Allah that He has granted him this grace, these favours, this subjugation, and this knowledge.

﴿And that you may be grateful﴾ (45:12). Allah then, through this Qur'an, guides man to be faithful to the Divine Being, to establish a connection with Him, and to understand that there is a relationship between you and this universe: you are a part of it, you move under one natural order, and both of you turn toward Allah alone.

Along with the specific mention of the subjugation of the seas, this whole universe has also been generally subjected to you: all the forces, blessings and beneficial things that lie between the earth and the heavens, which are helpful and supportive in the discharge of the duties of the office of vicegerency.

﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ (45:13). Everything in this universe belongs to Allah and comes from Him. He is its Creator and its Manager. He has subjected them, and has imposed upon them this small creature, man, whom Allah has endowed with the capacity to understand the temperament and laws of this universe, and who, by his own strength and power, subdues forces far greater than himself. All this is the favour and grace of Allah. In this there are signs and indications for this man and for those who reflect and ponder, provided they also use their reason to recognise that this universe and this man have a Creator who has given them all this by His special grace:

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ (45:13). This reflection and contemplation cannot be correct, comprehensive and deep until one strives to look behind these forces, these subjugated forces, toward the great power that created all these forces, that created man, and then made man aware of the secrets of these forces: what their secret is, and what their law of nature is. The nature of the universe and the nature of man are one, and there is a connection between the two. The result of this connection is that man acquired knowledge, acquired power and control, and subdued these forces and used them for his benefit. Had this connection not existed, man would have gained nothing at all from these things.

* * *

When the discussion reaches this point, and a believer arrives at the very heart of this universe, he comes to realise what the true source of power is, and that the true source of power is the awareness of the secrets and mysteries of this universe. Now the believers are guided to adopt nobility, lofty morals, magnanimity and tolerance, and to show mercy and sympathy toward the weak, the helpless and the ignorant who are deprived of this treasure and this abundant treasury of knowledge and recognition, because these people are deprived of these great truths. They do not observe the laws of nature of Allah, they do not seek the Divine practices (sunan Ilahiyyah) in history, and they are not acquainted with the secrets and mysteries of this universe; therefore they are also unaware of the greatness of this Creator.

In the scale of Allah there is a difference between the two. Allah has established this system of the heavens and the earth upon truth and justice, and in the design of this universe truth is the fundamental and foundational element.

Since Allah created human beings, only Allah's sharia can be free from ignorance, personal desires and shortcomings. This is because all people are Allah's servants. Allah is not a supporter of one and an opponent of another. Allah is free from ignorance, fault and desires. He knows best, and He is All-Subtle and All-Aware.

﴿And We preferred them over the worlds﴾ (45:16). At that central position, as bearers of divine guidance, they were then a nation superior to all the world, and the great proof of their excellence was that they were the bearers of the sharia, and they were given governance and prophethood.

In it there was nothing incomprehensible, complicated, crooked or deviating from the right path. Therefore the differences and sects that arose among them over this sharia had no justification. Their division was not because they did not understand the sharia and religion, or because they were ignorant and did not know the right thing and the truth.

﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾ (45:17). The differences that arose among them were made knowingly. Intense envy and hatred had arisen among them, and these differences were made amid mutual conflict and oppression of one another, despite the fact that they knew the correct thing.

In this way the matter becomes entirely clear: either there will be Allah's sharia or there will be the desires of those who do not know. There is no third option. Either there is the straight and upright sharia and highway, or there are the changing desires of people, and there is no third path between them. The people who abandon the sharia worship their own desires, because whatever exists apart from the sharia is the whim and lust of those who do not believe.

Allah warns the Prophet ﷺ not to obey the desires of those who do not know. If you did this, these people would be of no benefit to you against Allah. These people are friends of one another. Even if those who do not accept Allah's religion and sharia become close friends of one another and form an alliance, they cannot harm you in any way, because O Messenger, your Protector is Allah.

﴿Indeed, they will not avail you at all against Allah. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the ally of the righteous﴾ (45:19). Thus, O Prophet, We have placed you on a clear path (the sharia) in the matter of religion. So follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. They cannot avail you at all against Allah. The wrongdoers are allies of one another, and the protector of the righteous is Allah.

That is, on one side is the sharia, based on knowledge and wisdom, and on the other side are base desires, based on ignorance and being the jahiliyyah. A caller (da'i) should follow the sharia and leave aside all personal desires. It is the duty of the caller not to deviate from the sharia, because people with personal desires cannot provide any help against Allah. Rather, they oppose the caller, and they all unite in opposition, and in opposing the sharia they support and assist one another. Therefore the caller should not expect anything from wrongdoers and ignorant people. Furthermore, these wrongdoers cannot help a caller either, because that is against their desires. Yet they are so weak that they cannot even harm the true caller, because the caller's protector and guardian is Allah, and no one can confront the one whose protector is Allah. Human beings are weak and frail, having no power of their own, whereas the friends of Allah are the Muslims, and they are strong.

A further comment on this decisive statement: the Qur'an speaks in clear and decisive terms, and through these clear words of the Qur'an, certainty is attained, which gives a person insight and guidance.

﴿These are insights from your Lord for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾ (45:20). The Qur'an is described as insight for people. This means that the Qur'an contains deep insight and light. The Qur'an in itself is insight and light, just as insight and light are means for people to see and understand, so the Qur'an in itself is insight and guidance, and it is in itself mercy. However, these qualities will appear in the Qur'an, and benefits will be obtained from it, only when a taste of certainty is created in a person. A person must attain such certainty that there is not even a shadow of doubt in them. There should be no restlessness and no disquiet in the heart. When the heart attains certainty and complete conviction, there is no longer any wavering in it. It no longer hesitates or drifts here and there. Its path becomes clear. It sees its destination raised high on the horizon. Its purpose becomes fixed, and its method of work becomes firm and established. Then the Qur'an becomes for it a light of insight, becomes guidance and becomes mercy, provided that the certainty is firm.

After this statement, that the wrongdoers are friends of one another, and Allah is the protector of the righteous, and that the Qur'an is a light of insight for the Qur'an's sake and guidance and mercy for those who have certainty, it is said that there is a fundamental difference between those who commit evil deeds and those who do righteous deeds, that is, the believers, and that both cannot have one station with Allah, nor can both receive the same judgement. In the scale of Allah there is a difference between the two. Allah has established this system of the heavens and the earth upon truth and justice, and in the design of this universe truth is the fundamental and foundational element.

Perhaps the "evildoers" here refers to the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) who turned away from their own scripture and committed wrongdoing. Yet they continued to think that they were true believers. Indeed, they regard themselves as equal to the believers, even while they commit evil deeds and the believers perform good works. The question is whether these two groups can be equal in the sight of God, whether in the matter of this world or in a comparison of the Hereafter. This verse may also state a general principle: according to God's standards, those who do good and those who do evil cannot be equal, neither in this world nor in the reckoning of the Hereafter. The scales of the believers will be heavier here and will also be heavier in the Hereafter. This principle holds the place of the backbone in the design of God's universe. The creation of this entire universe rests on truth, and the formation of the Shari'ah also rests on truth. The thing on which this universe is sustained is balance and moderation, and human life is likewise established on this principle, namely justice, which is expressed by distinguishing between those who do good and those who do evil. Every person has been given the recompense or punishment for what he did, whether he was righteous or went astray, so that justice may be done to all people.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ (45:22). The meaning is that in the original design of this universe, truth is the fundamental element. Just as there is truth within the universe, so there is truth within the Shari'ah, and on the Day of Reckoning the reckoning will be made on this same truth. This meaning and theme recur again and again in the Qur'an, because it is one of the fundamental principles of the Islamic conception of life. All its branches are based on this principle. The human self, the horizons of the universe and the Islamic Shari'ah are all founded on this truth. Verse 23

When a person abandons the great Islamic principle of following the Shariah, the Holy Qur'an vividly portrays his condition. This person is subservient to his ever-changing desires. He prostrates before his desires and is their obedient servant. His ideas, his rulings, his thinking and his actions are all shaped from the angle of his desires. He worships them in the same way that someone worships an idol. He runs after the signals of his desires. The Qur'an depicts such people with great disapproval.

﴿Have you then considered the one who takes his own desire as his god?﴾ (45:23) Have you ever seen such a person? He is a strange creature, worthy of being watched as a spectacle. Such a person proves himself deserving of misguidance before Allah. Now Allah does not even send down the mercy of guidance upon such a person, because there is no longer any place for guidance in his heart, since he constantly worships his desire at every moment.

﴿And Allah has sent him astray knowingly﴾ (45:23) This has two meanings. One is that Allah, knowing his condition, cast him into misguidance, because he had become deserving of it. The other is that despite his own knowledge and awareness, he was cast into misguidance, since his knowledge and understanding did not prevent him from taking his desires as gods. ﴿And has sealed over his hearing and his heart and placed over his sight a covering﴾ (45:23) Consequently, all the openings through which light used to enter were closed, and the faculties through which guidance could enter a person's heart and mind became useless. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ (45:23) Whoever takes heed remains wise and becomes alert, is freed from the snare of his own desires, and proceeds upon a clear and steady path, one upon which those who walk have never gone astray.

Lesson No. 236: Explanation of the Verses

24 to 37

Verses 24 to 26

Their view about the Hour was based on such short-sightedness that, in their opinion, life was just this much which they could see passing on this earth. One generation is born and keeps passing away. Apparently death is nothing except that time passes and we die, and time keeps folding up. As if it is time that makes all decisions, and it is time that brings death upon them, and they die.

This was a superficial view. They adopted it merely by looking at outward conditions; they made no effort at all to seek out the secrets and mysteries behind life. The question was: where did life come from? And who is it that takes life back? Death does not arrive after some fixed number of days, such that they could link death with time. Children also die like the elderly, and healthy people also die, just as sick people die. Strong people die just like the weak. Therefore, if one looks with a deep eye, the connection of time with death and life does not exist, provided that one wishes to know the reality of death. So it was said:

"And they have no knowledge of this; they merely conjecture" (45:24). In truth, they have no knowledge in this matter; they speak only on the basis of assumption. They are walking on the wooden legs of conjecture and estimation. Their thoughts are dim and their impressions are blurred. They are not based on deep reflection, nor are they based on any knowledge. They have no grasp of the realities of this universe. They look only at the superficial causes of the conditions of life and death that overtake man; the real causes are hidden from their sight. They have only ascertained this much: after many days pass, man becomes weak and dies.

"And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is: bring back our fathers, if you are truthful" (45:25). Their statement is also based on very superficial thinking, and before this they did not study the laws of nature of this universe. The system that Allah has ordained for life and death in this world, and the secrets and mysteries that He has fixed for them, they have not pondered deeply. There is deep wisdom operating within it. People come into this world and keep coming and going. In the system of Allah they are being given here an opportunity for action. After death they will be raised again at a fixed time, and they will have to give an account of what they did here. Therefore, before the gathering and resurrection, they cannot be raised here according to the system of Allah. To raise them here before the fixed Day of Resurrection would be contrary to the wisdom of the trial. Some people propose that every paper be leaked before its time. But Allah has His own work and system, and His own wisdom and scheme, upon which this entire universe is established. Therefore, Allah's entire scheme cannot be changed according to this foolish proposal. Instead of giving a reasonable answer to the Qur'anic argument, they simply say:

"Bring back our fathers, if you are truthful" (45:25). The question is: why would Allah bring back their forefathers before the appointed time that He has fixed for this entire universe? Merely so that they may be convinced that Allah can raise the dead again? The question is: is Allah not, in accordance with His sunnah, raising up life before their very eyes at every moment and every instant?

"Say: Allah gives you life, then He causes you to die, then He will gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt" (45:26). This is indeed the miracle which they want to see in the bringing back of their forefathers. Is it not taking place before their eyes? Exactly the same miracle. It is Allah who is creating human beings continually. It is He who causes death. So what is so strange in the matter that Allah will gather them again on the Day of Resurrection? Why then are they falling into doubt about it? The thing with which they are being warned has its parallel in their own lives.

"But most people do not know" (45:26). Allah is the controller of everything in the heavens and the earth. He is the creator of everything. He is also capable of creating again, since He created them the first time, and you acknowledge that this is so.

But instead of rational proofs, Allah presents before them a scene:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 45, verse 35:

Verse 35 (1)

Now the curtain falls on the announcement of their final end: they are left in Hell forever, no excuse is sought from them, and no requests for forgiveness are entertained.

Verse 35 (2)

It is as though, with these words, we hear harsh sounds, and the gates of Hell are closed upon them forever. Here the scene comes to an end, and no change or alteration takes place in this condition.

At this point, the voices of praise and glorification of Allah rise. After this introduction and scene, the final words of the surah are extremely impactful.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 45, verses 36–37:

Verses 36–37

The greatness of Allah and the exaltation of Allah are proclaimed. In the heavens He is Great, and on the earth too it is He who is Great. He is the ruler of mankind and He is the ruler of the jinn. He is also the creator of beasts and birds. In short, whatever is in this universe belongs to Allah, and all of it is under the supervision of one Lord. It is Allah who is the Governor of the universe and the Lord of the universe.

The praise of Allah and the voice of His magnificence rise high. It is proclaimed that in this universe greatness belongs to Allah alone. In comparison to Him, every great one becomes small, and ... here, the one who is bent on his knees. Every rebel here bows in submission, before the Absolute Lord and the Absolute Greatest.

With this greatness, this lordship, this power, this wisdom and this governance, He is established as the Victorious.

﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (45:37). ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds!﴾
